title: Fugen Engine show document (show.json)
description:
The authored screenplay of a generative piece, as data. Read by `spex-show` (crates/spex-show/src/model.rs); compiled by `spex show-build` into a `show-resolved.json` (see show-resolved.schema.json) plus the mesh bundles every scene needs.

Two properties of this format are load-bearing and are stated here rather than left to readers to infer.

FIRST: TIME IS AUTHORED IN BARS, NOT SECONDS. The piece is written at a fixed tempo (84 bpm, 4/4 by default) and sets itself the rule that every cut lands on a bar line. In seconds that rule is unenforceable — one bar is 20/7 s, and 2.857142857 is a bar only if you type enough sevens. So a shot states `durationBars` and seconds are derived: `durationBars * beatsPerBar * 60 / bpm`. The canonical cut is 84 bars, which is 240.000 s exactly, and is exact only because 84 x 20/7 is.

SECOND: A CUT IS A SELECTION, NOT A SPEED CHANGE. The 4:00, 10:00 and 60:00 versions are three resolutions of this one document, not three edits. `tier` decides which shots a given cut contains at all; `scaling` decides how the ones that survive respond to the time available. Nothing is ever played faster or slower — the tempo is the same in every cut, because the music is the same music.

Colours in `palette` are LINEAR rgb, the same convention as mesh.json, for the same reason: three.js reads raw components as linear and converting again would brighten everything about 2.2x.

version.description: Bumped when a change would make an older document read wrong rather than merely incomplete.

archiveSignature.description: The Iunctura Archiv signature, e.g. "IA-2026-002". Carried into every resolved output and shown in the credits: a generative piece with no fixed frames still has one identity.

tempo.description: Defaults to 84 bpm in 4/4 when absent.

baseDurationBars.description: The canonical cut, in bars. 84 at the default tempo — 240.000 s.

seed.description: Default edition seed. Every random choice in the piece descends from this one number, which is what makes an edition reproducible from its signature alone.

palette.description: Named LINEAR rgb triples, 0..1. Named rather than inline so "Terminalgrün" means one colour across the whole piece.

scenes.description: Every piece of geometry the show can address. A shot names scenes by id; it never names a file.

prefix.description: Instance-id prefix, e.g. "monolith". A scene's bundle numbers its own instances `<part>/<n>` (`3010/0`, `3710/7`), so the addressable id is `<prefix>/<part>/<n>` — `monolith/3010/0`, with TWO separators. Track targets are globs over these, and a `*` does not cross a `/` (which is what makes `flag/dk/tile-*` mean anything), so "every instance of this scene" is `monolith/**` and `monolith/*` matches nothing at all, silently. The resolver expands each glob to an instance-index list exactly once at load — never per frame, because at Atlas scale that would be a string match per brick per track per frame.

path.description: A real .ldr file in this repository, e.g. "ldraw-scenes/monolith.ldr".

source.description: Four kinds because four different milestones produce geometry, and the document should not have to care which one a scene came from.

id.description: e.g. "A1-S04". Unique across the whole document: cues, the HUD and seeking all address shots by id.

weight.description: Proportional share of the movement's stretchable time. Meaningless for `scaling: "fixed"`.

scaling.description: fixed — the duration never changes, in any cut. The Kick is two beats in the 4:00 and two beats in the 60:00, because a flash that lasts ten seconds is not a flash. stretch — scales with the cut, clamped to minBars/maxBars. repeat — the body loops N times; N scales, one pass does not.

tier.description: 1 = present in every cut. 2 = added by cuts of 10 minutes or more. 3 = added by cuts of an hour or more.

unitBars.description: One pass. The Atlas unit is 2 bars.

repeat.description: Required when `scaling` is "repeat", forbidden otherwise — a repeat shot that does not say what one pass is has no resolvable duration.

scenes.description: Scene ids active in this shot. Every id must be defined in the document's top-level `scenes`.

note.description: Free-form direction, carried into the resolved output so the piece documents itself — shown by the director HUD (?director=1).

easing.description: `step` is instant, and is not a rounding of a very fast fade. A1-S03's edge lines arrive in ONE frame; a fade would make legibility gradual, and the whole shot is about it not being gradual.

t.description: Normalised shot-local time, so a keyframe survives retiming into any cut. The resolver turns it into an absolute `timeSec`.

snapToBeat.description: Snap the resolved time to the nearest beat rather than keeping proportional time. This is how a landing brick lands ON the beat instead of near it.

rotation.description: Euler XYZ in degrees. Ignored when `quaternion` is present.

vec3.description: Millimetres, +Y up — the same frame mesh.json uses.

track.description: Keyframed animation of one thing. `target` is a glob over scene-prefixed instance ids, resolved once at load. `*` matches within one path segment and `**` crosses separators — so `monolith/**` is every brick of the monolith, `flag/dk/tile-*` is one segment of a flag's ids, and `monolith/*` is a common mistake that matches nothing (see `sceneRef.prefix`).

property.description: A closed set on purpose: an open string would let a show reference a property no renderer has, and the failure would be silent.
The parameters M58's post chain actually exposes. Same closed-set reasoning.

oneOf.description: The mesh<->point crossfade: 0 is the mesh, 1 is the point swarm. A1-S03 is the centre of the whole piece and it is exactly this track.

mode.description: Each mode requires its own block and forbids the others' — a `mode` with no matching block is an error, not a silent default, because the fallback would be a static camera and a static camera looks deliberate.

exponentialZoom.description: The Kick: distance from `from` to `to` on a log scale, 10^4 over two beats.

payload.description: Free-form, interpreted by whatever consumes that `kind`.

required.description: Attribution that must appear regardless of cut length — the LDraw library's CCAL terms among them. Not stretchable, not tier-gated: a licence condition is not editorial material.
